title: Login via browser URL and SSO layer shows logon screen
description: Verifies that entering the application URL in a browser launches the application and presents the logon screen, and that login is performed via the Single Sign on Layer. This ensures access to the call centre terminal starts from the supported entry point. Automation: MEDIUM (UI + SSO dependency).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, when I type the application URL in the browser and launch the application, I should be taken to the logon screen, and the login path should be through the Single Sign on Layer.
prerequisites:
1) Test environment is deployed and reachable over network.
2) A valid application URL is available for the call centre terminal (synthetic/non-production).
3) Single Sign on Layer is configured and available for this environment.
4) A test user exists and is enabled for SSO (e.g., user id 'cc_user_01').
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a supported web browser on a clean session (no existing app tabs) and confirm no existing session for the application is active.
2. Type the application URL in the browser address bar and press ENTER; observe that the browser starts loading the application.
3. Wait for the page to finish loading; observe that the application is launched.
4. Observe that the logon screen is displayed (as per the call centre logging on screen).
5. On the displayed logon screen, confirm the presence of login fields (login ID and password) and a Login action control is visible.
6. Confirm on this flow that login is routed through the Single Sign on Layer (e.g., SSO-branded login layer/page is presented as part of the login journey).
7. Refresh the browser page (F5); observe that the same logon screen is presented again (no unexpected navigation away from logon).
8. Close the browser tab; observe that the application page is closed (cleanup).
expectedResult:
1) The application launches after the URL is entered and displays the logon screen.
2) The login flow is presented through the Single Sign on Layer (SSO), with no alternative non-SSO login path shown in this flow.
3) Refreshing the page keeps the user at the logon screen (until authenticated).

sourceCitation.excerpt: Type the URL in the browser to logon to the application.

title: Login screen supports Hebrew and English language selection
description: Verifies that the logon screen provides a language selector with the two documented options (Hebrew and English). This is critical for multilingual call centre operations. Automation: MEDIUM (UI assertions, language rendering).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user at the logon screen, I can select the application language from Hebrew and English before proceeding.
prerequisites:
1) Application URL is reachable.
2) Logon screen is available (user is not authenticated).
3) Environment has both Hebrew and English language packs/config enabled.
4) Test user credentials exist (synthetic).
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a supported browser and navigate to the application URL; observe the logon screen is displayed.
2. Locate the language selection control on the logon screen; observe it is present and interactable.
3. Open the language options; observe that both language choices are displayed.
4. Select English; observe that the selected value shows as English.
5. Verify the logon screen labels are displayed in English after selection (visible UI language change).
6. Open the language selector again; observe options remain available.
7. Select Hebrew; observe that the selected value shows as Hebrew.
8. Verify the logon screen labels are displayed in Hebrew after selection (visible UI language change).
9. Close the browser tab to end the session (cleanup).
expectedResult:
1) The logon screen provides language selection with exactly the documented options: Hebrew and English.
2) Selecting English/Hebrew updates the displayed logon screen language accordingly.
3) Language selection is possible before login is performed.

sourceCitation.excerpt: select the language from the options available (Hebrew and English).

title: Keyboard navigation: TAB advances and SHIFT+TAB goes to previous field
description: Verifies accessibility/keyboard navigation on the logon screen: TAB moves focus forward and SHIFT+TAB moves focus backward between fields. This supports efficient call centre workflows and keyboard-only usage. Automation: MEDIUM (UI focus order checks).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, I can navigate the login fields using TAB and SHIFT+TAB to move forward and backward across fields on the logon screen.
prerequisites:
1) Application URL is reachable.
2) User is currently logged out and logon screen is displayed.
3) Browser allows keyboard focus indicators (no extensions disabling focus outlines).
stepsToPerform:
1. Open the browser and navigate to the application URL; observe the logon screen is displayed.
2. Click once inside the login ID field; observe the cursor/focus is in the login ID field.
3. Press TAB; observe focus moves to the next field on the logon screen.
4. Press TAB again; observe focus moves to the next interactive element after that field.
5. Press SHIFT+TAB; observe focus moves back to the previous field.
6. Press SHIFT+TAB again; observe focus moves back to the login ID field.
7. Without using the mouse, continue pressing TAB until the Login action control is focused; observe the focus indicator reaches Login.
8. Close the browser tab (cleanup).
expectedResult:
1) Pressing TAB moves focus to the next field/control on the logon screen.
2) Pressing SHIFT+TAB moves focus to the previous field/control on the logon screen.
3) The user can reach the Login action using only keyboard navigation.

sourceCitation.location: Getting Started > Logging on Note (Lines L536-L540)
sourceCitation.excerpt: Press the TAB key to move to the next field and press SHIFT+TAB to move to the previous field.

title: First-time login uses default password provided by admin
description: Verifies the documented first-time login behavior where the user uses a default password provided by the admin. This ensures onboarding aligns with the specified authentication approach. Automation: LOW-MEDIUM (requires first-time user state).
testDescription: As a first-time Call Centre user, I log in using the default password provided by the admin and proceed into the application flow.
prerequisites:
1) A test user exists that is marked as first-time login (no prior successful login recorded) (e.g., login ID 'cc_first_01').
2) Admin-provided default password is available for this test user (synthetic, e.g., 'TempPwd#12345').
3) SSO layer is available.
4) Application URL is reachable.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a supported browser and navigate to the application URL; observe the logon screen is displayed.
2. In the login ID field, enter the first-time test login ID 'cc_first_01'; observe the value is entered.
3. In the password field, enter the admin-provided default password 'TempPwd#12345'; observe the value is entered (masked).
4. If language selection is present, select English; observe English is selected.
5. Click the Login button; observe authentication is attempted through the SSO layer.
6. Wait for the post-authentication navigation; observe that the next screen is displayed.
7. Observe that the Customer Authentication screen appears after login.
8. Close the browser tab to end the session (cleanup).
expectedResult:
1) The first-time user can enter the default password provided by admin and proceed through login.
2) After successful login, the system navigates forward and displays the Customer Authentication screen.
3) No additional unspecified steps are required beyond entering login ID and the default password.

sourceCitation.excerpt: If logging on for the first time, type the default password, admin provides.

title: Press ENTER as alternative to clicking Login
description: Verifies that pressing ENTER on the logon screen triggers login as an alternative to clicking the Login button. This supports keyboard-driven workflows. Automation: MEDIUM.
testDescription: As a Call Centre user on the logon screen, I can submit login by pressing ENTER instead of clicking Login and reach the Customer Authentication screen.
prerequisites:
1) A valid test user exists for SSO login (e.g., 'cc_user_01' with password 'Pwd#12345!').
2) Application URL is reachable and user is logged out.
3) SSO layer is available.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a supported browser and navigate to the application URL; observe the logon screen is displayed.
2. Enter login ID 'cc_user_01' in the login ID field; observe it is populated.
3. Enter password 'Pwd#12345!' in the password field; observe it is masked.
4. Select English as the language (if not already selected); observe English is shown.
5. Place focus in the password field (or any field on the form); observe the caret/focus is visible.
6. Press ENTER; observe the system attempts to submit the login form.
7. Wait for navigation; observe that the Customer Authentication screen appears.
8. Close the browser tab (cleanup).
expectedResult:
1) Pressing ENTER submits the login action without requiring a mouse click.
2) On successful authentication, the system navigates to the Customer Authentication screen.
3) The behavior matches the documented alternative to clicking Login.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Click Login. Alternatively, press ENTER.

title: Post-login shows Customer Authentication screen
description: Verifies that after a successful login, the application displays the Customer Authentication screen. This is a critical gateway step before customer-specific operations. Automation: MEDIUM.
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, after logging in successfully, I am taken to the Customer Authentication screen.
prerequisites:
1) Valid test user exists and can authenticate via SSO (e.g., 'cc_user_02' / 'Pwd#12345!').
2) Application URL is reachable.
3) SSO layer is available.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a supported browser and navigate to the application URL; observe the logon screen is displayed.
2. Enter login ID 'cc_user_02'; observe the value is entered.
3. Enter password 'Pwd#12345!'; observe the password field masks input.
4. Select English language; observe English is selected.
5. Click Login; observe authentication is initiated.
6. Wait for successful authentication to complete; observe a post-login page load occurs.
7. Verify the Customer Authentication screen is displayed (screen header/section indicates customer authentication).
8. Verify that the Customer Authentication screen contains fields/controls used for authentication (e.g., Service Mode, identification inputs, Authenticate action).
9. Close the browser tab (cleanup).
expectedResult:
1) Successful login transitions the user to the Customer Authentication screen.
2) Customer Authentication inputs and actions are visible on that screen.
3) The screen is shown immediately after login as documented.

sourceCitation.excerpt: The Customer Authentication screen appears.

title: Customer Authentication supports Service Mode Phone/Fax/Email
description: Verifies that the Customer Authentication screen provides Service Mode selection with the documented options (Phone, Fax, Email). This supports correct recording of customer contact channel. Automation: MEDIUM.
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, I can select the Service Mode on the Customer Authentication screen from the available options Phone, Fax, and Email.
prerequisites:
1) Valid test user exists for login.
2) Application URL is reachable; SSO is available.
3) Customer Authentication screen is accessible after login.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open browser and navigate to the application URL; observe the logon screen.
2. Log in with test user 'cc_user_03' / 'Pwd#12345!'; observe login completes.
3. Observe the Customer Authentication screen is displayed.
4. Locate the Service Mode field/control; observe it is present.
5. Open the Service Mode options; observe the available options list.
6. Select Phone; observe Service Mode displays Phone.
7. Re-open Service Mode and select Fax; observe Service Mode displays Fax.
8. Re-open Service Mode and select Email; observe Service Mode displays Email.
9. Do not proceed with Authenticate; close the browser tab (cleanup).
expectedResult:
1) Service Mode field is present on Customer Authentication screen.
2) The available Service Mode options include Phone, Fax, and Email.
3) Selecting each option updates the Service Mode value displayed.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Select Service Mode (Phone, Fax, Email).

title: Authenticate using Identification Type + Identification Number
description: Verifies customer authentication using Identification Type and Identification Number and that the flow proceeds to show the Portfolio List after clicking Authenticate. This ensures the primary customer identification mechanism works. Automation: MEDIUM (requires seeded customer data).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, I authenticate a customer by providing Identification Type and Identification Number and clicking Authenticate, resulting in a Portfolio List display.
prerequisites:
1) Valid test user exists for login.
2) A test customer record exists with an Identification Type and Identification Number (synthetic), and has at least one linked portfolio.
3) Example synthetic customer identity: Identification Type='National Id', Identification Number='999999999' (non-real).
4) Application URL and SSO layer are available.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open browser and navigate to the application URL; observe the logon screen.
2. Log in using test user 'cc_user_04' / 'Pwd#12345!'; observe login succeeds.
3. Observe the Customer Authentication screen is displayed.
4. Set Service Mode to Phone; observe the selected value is shown.
5. Set Identification Type to 'National Id'; observe the selected value is shown.
6. Enter Identification Number '999999999'; observe the input is accepted in the field.
7. Click Authenticate button; observe the system processes the authentication request.
8. Observe that a Portfolio List is displayed with reference number.
9. From the Portfolio List, select one portfolio row; observe the row is selected.
10. Click Submit; observe submission is accepted (end of authentication journey).
11. Close the browser tab (cleanup).
expectedResult:
1) The system accepts Identification Type and Identification Number inputs and proceeds on Authenticate.
2) After clicking Authenticate, "A Portfolio List is displayed with reference number".
3) The user can select an appropriate portfolio from the displayed list and submit.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Provide Identification Type  (National Id/ Passport Id and all the other option which customer would use at the time of onboarding) and Identification Number.

title: Authenticate using Portfolio Reference Number as alternative
description: Verifies the alternate customer authentication method using Portfolio Reference Number, and that clicking Authenticate results in a Portfolio List display. This provides an alternative lookup path for call centre efficiency. Automation: MEDIUM (requires seeded portfolio reference).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, I authenticate by providing a Portfolio Reference Number instead of Identification details, then click Authenticate to view the Portfolio List.
prerequisites:
1) Valid test user exists for login.
2) A test portfolio exists with a known Portfolio Reference Number (synthetic) and is searchable.
3) Example synthetic Portfolio Reference Number: 'PRN-TEST-000123'.
4) Application URL and SSO layer are available.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open browser and navigate to the application URL; observe the logon screen.
2. Log in using test user 'cc_user_05' / 'Pwd#12345!'; observe login succeeds.
3. Observe the Customer Authentication screen is displayed.
4. Set Service Mode to Email; observe Service Mode shows Email.
5. Leave Identification Type and Identification Number empty (do not enter values); observe fields remain blank.
6. Enter Portfolio Reference Number 'PRN-TEST-000123'; observe the field is populated.
7. Click Authenticate button; observe the system processes the authentication request.
8. Observe that a Portfolio List is displayed with reference number.
9. Select an appropriate portfolio row in the Portfolio List; observe selection is applied.
10. Click Submit; observe the selection is submitted.
11. Close the browser tab (cleanup).
expectedResult:
1) Customer Authentication supports Portfolio Reference Number as an alternative input path.
2) Clicking Authenticate with a Portfolio Reference Number results in a Portfolio List display.
3) The user can select a portfolio from the list and submit.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Alternatively, provide the Portfolio Reference Number.

title: Reset button clears Customer Authentication inputs
description: Verifies that using Reset on the Customer Authentication screen clears user-entered authentication inputs, preventing accidental reuse of prior customer identifiers. Automation: MEDIUM.
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, after entering values on the Customer Authentication screen, I can click Reset to clear the entered inputs before proceeding.
prerequisites:
1) Valid test user exists for login.
2) Application URL and SSO layer are available.
3) Customer Authentication screen is accessible after login.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open browser and navigate to the application URL; observe the logon screen.
2. Log in using test user 'cc_user_06' / 'Pwd#12345!'; observe login succeeds.
3. Observe the Customer Authentication screen is displayed.
4. Select Service Mode as Fax; observe the field shows Fax.
5. Select Identification Type as 'Passport Id'; observe the field shows the selected type.
6. Enter Identification Number 'P-TEST-123456' (synthetic); observe it is populated.
7. Enter Portfolio Reference Number 'PRN-TEST-000999' (synthetic); observe it is populated.
8. Click Reset; observe the inputs on the Customer Authentication screen are cleared.
9. Verify Service Mode, Identification Type, Identification Number, and Portfolio Reference Number are empty/default (no previously entered values remain visible).
10. Close the browser tab (cleanup).
expectedResult:
1) Clicking Reset clears the entered Customer Authentication input values (e.g., Identification Number and Portfolio Reference Number).
2) After Reset, the screen is ready for fresh input (no prior customer identifiers remain visible).
3) No authentication action is performed as a result of Reset alone.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Click Authenticate button.

title: Portfolio List displays all portfolios linked to search and requires selection + Submit
description: Verifies that after customer authentication, the Portfolio List shows all portfolios linked to the search and the user must select one portfolio before submitting. This ensures the correct customer portfolio context is established before proceeding. Automation: MEDIUM (UI list verification and selection).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, I authenticate a customer using identification details to retrieve the Portfolio List, confirm all linked portfolios are displayed, select the appropriate portfolio, and submit to proceed.
prerequisites: 1) Call Centre user account is active and can log in via SSO. 2) Test customer exists with multiple portfolios linked to the same Identification Type/Identification Number search. 3) Application URL is reachable in test environment.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a browser and navigate to the Call Centre application URL; verify the logon screen is displayed.
2. Enter a valid test Login ID and Password, select a language option, and click Login; verify the Customer Authentication screen appears.
3. In Customer Authentication, select Service Mode = Phone; verify the selection is accepted in the Service Mode field.
4. Enter Identification Type = National Id and Identification Number = TEST-NID-0001, then click Authenticate; verify the system proceeds to display the Portfolio List.
5. On the Portfolio List screen, verify that multiple portfolio rows are displayed for the search (i.e., all portfolios linked to the search are visible as a list).
6. Attempt to proceed without selecting any portfolio and observe the screen state; verify that a portfolio is still not chosen (no row is highlighted/selected).
7. Select (highlight) the appropriate portfolio row (e.g., the one matching the intended Reference shown in the list); verify the row remains selected.
8. Click Submit; verify the workflow continues beyond the Portfolio List (Integrated Login step appears next).
expectedResult:
1) Portfolio List is displayed after clicking Authenticate.
2) The Portfolio List shows all portfolios linked to the search as rows in the list.
3) User can select the appropriate portfolio and click Submit to proceed to the next step (Integrated Login).

sourceCitation.excerpt: All portfolio linked to the search will be displayed, User must select the appropriate one and click Submit.

title: Integrated login requires selecting Trading from three options
description: Verifies that for integrated login, the user must choose the Trading option from the available options before reaching the Trading screen. This ensures correct functional context selection for trading operations. Automation: MEDIUM (UI selection and navigation).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user completing authentication and portfolio selection, I am presented with an integrated login choice and must select Trading from the three options to enter the trading module.
prerequisites: 1) Call Centre user account is active and can log in via SSO. 2) Test customer authentication succeeds and returns at least one portfolio. 3) At least one portfolio can be selected and submitted to reach Integrated Login.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open the application URL in a browser; verify the logon screen appears.
2. Enter valid Login ID and Password, select a language, and click Login; verify the Customer Authentication screen appears.
3. Select Service Mode and provide Identification Type/Identification Number, then click Authenticate; verify the Portfolio List is displayed.
4. Select a portfolio from the Portfolio List and click Submit; verify the Integrated Login screen appears.
5. Verify the Integrated Login screen displays three options (including Trading).
6. Select Trading; verify Trading is visibly selected (radio/selection indicator changes).
7. Confirm/continue from the integrated login selection (as applicable on the screen); verify navigation proceeds.
8. Verify the Trading screen is displayed after selecting Trading.
expectedResult:
1) After portfolio Submit, Integrated Login screen is displayed.
2) Trading can be selected from the three options.
3) After selecting Trading, the system navigates to the Trading screen.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Since the login is Integrated, the user must select Trading from the three options

title: Trading screen shows functionalities as tiles and allows opening by clicking tile
description: Verifies that the Trading screen renders available functionalities as tiles and that the user can open a function by clicking the respective tile. This protects usability and discoverability of core trading workflows. Automation: MEDIUM (UI tile presence + navigation).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user entering the Trading module, I see functionalities presented as tiles and can launch a chosen function by clicking its tile.
prerequisites: 1) Call Centre user account is active and can log in via SSO. 2) Customer authentication + portfolio selection is successful. 3) Integrated login selection can be completed by choosing Trading.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open the application URL; verify the logon screen appears.
2. Log in with valid credentials and select a language; verify the Customer Authentication screen appears.
3. Authenticate the customer (Service Mode + Identification details or Portfolio Reference Number) and click Authenticate; verify the Portfolio List is shown.
4. Select a portfolio and click Submit; verify Integrated Login appears.
5. Select Trading from the options; verify navigation continues.
6. Verify the Trading screen appears and the functionalities are displayed as tiles.
7. Click the Dashboard tile on the Trading screen; verify the Dashboard screen opens.
8. Navigate back to the Trading screen (e.g., using available navigation controls); verify the tiles are visible again.
9. Click another visible tile (any function tile present); verify the corresponding function screen/window opens.
expectedResult:
1) Trading screen appears and displays functionalities as tiles.
2) Clicking a tile opens the respective function.
3) Dashboard tile click opens the Dashboard screen.

sourceCitation.excerpt: The Trading screen appears (all the functionalities are shown as tiles). You can choose any function by clicking the respective tiles on the Trading screen

title: Menu bar contains Home, Market View, Orders, Account & Portfolio, Reports, Research & News and Injob Activities
description: Verifies that the Menu bar displays the specified main menu items. This ensures consistent navigation entry points for the Call Centre terminal. Automation: HIGH (UI text presence assertions).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, I verify the Menu bar shows the required top-level menus for navigation across modules.
prerequisites: 1) Call Centre user account is active and can log in via SSO. 2) Trading Dashboard/UI loads successfully after login (customer selection not required for viewing the interface elements).
stepsToPerform:
1. Open the application URL in a browser; verify the logon screen appears.
2. Enter valid Login ID and Password, select a language, and click Login; verify the Customer Authentication screen appears.
3. Proceed into Call Centre operations without selecting a customer (do not authenticate a customer); verify the main terminal interface loads.
4. Locate the Menu bar on the screen; verify it is visible.
5. Verify the Menu bar includes Home.
6. Verify the Menu bar includes Market View and Orders.
7. Verify the Menu bar includes Account & Portfolio and Reports.
8. Verify the Menu bar includes Research & News and Injob Activities.
9. Click each of the listed menu items one by one; verify each click opens its corresponding menu (dropdown/section) without error.
expectedResult:
1) Menu bar is visible on the terminal UI.
2) Menu bar displays: Home, Market View, Orders, Account & Portfolio, Reports, Research & News and Injob Activities.
3) Each menu item is clickable and opens its menu section.

sourceCitation.excerpt: The Menu bar displays main menu, which includes Home, Market View, Orders, Account & Portfolio, Reports, Research & News and Injob Activities.

title: Title area displays Bank Name and logged-in call centre user name
description: Verifies that the Title area shows the Bank Name and the logged-in call centre user name. This supports operator accountability and reduces operational risk of acting in the wrong session. Automation: MEDIUM (UI text assertion may vary by environment).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, after logging in I should see the Bank Name and my user name in the title area of the terminal UI.
prerequisites: 1) Call Centre user account is active and has a known display name (e.g., 'CCUser_Auto01'). 2) Application URL is reachable and login succeeds.

2. Enter Login ID = CCUser_Auto01 and Password = ******** (synthetic), select a language, and click Login; verify login completes and the terminal UI loads.
3. Locate the Title area on the screen; verify it is visible.
4. Verify the Title area contains the screen title as Bank Name.
5. Verify the Title area contains the name of the logged in call centre user (matching CCUser_Auto01 display name).
6. Refresh the page once (browser refresh) and re-load the UI; verify the Title area is still shown.
7. Re-verify Bank Name is displayed in the Title area.
8. Re-verify the logged-in call centre user name is still displayed and unchanged for this session.
expectedResult:

2) Title area shows the screen title as Bank Name.

sourceCitation.excerpt: The Title area shows the screen title as Bank Name and the name of the logged in call centre user.

title: Toolbar buttons navigate to screens such as mutual fund and buy/sell order entry

title: Dashboard/Market watch/In-job/News accessible without selecting customer
description: Verifies that a Call Centre user can access Dashboard and other non-customer-specific functions (market watch, In-job activities, News) without selecting a customer. This supports call-centre operations that do not require customer context. Automation: MEDIUM (UI access checks).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, I log in and, without authenticating/selecting any customer, access Dashboard, Market Watch, In-job activities, and News.
prerequisites: 1) Call Centre user account is active and can log in. 2) Application modules Dashboard, Market View, Injob Activities, and Research & News are enabled in the environment.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open the application URL; verify the logon screen appears.
2. Log in with valid credentials and select a language; verify the Customer Authentication screen appears.
3. Do not authenticate a customer (leave Identification/Portfolio fields unused) and proceed to Call Centre operations as allowed; verify the main terminal UI loads.
4. From the available navigation, open Dashboard; verify the Dashboard screen is displayed.
5. From the Menu bar, open Market View and select Market Watch; verify the Market Watch screen opens.
6. From the Menu bar, open Injob Activities; verify an Injob Activities screen/menu is accessible.
7. From the Menu bar, open Research & News; verify News is accessible.
8. Confirm that no customer selection/authentication step was performed during this journey; verify the user remained in non-customer context while accessing these functions.
expectedResult:
1) Dashboard is accessible without selecting a customer.
2) Market watch is accessible without selecting a customer.
3) In-job activities and News are accessible without selecting a customer.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Call Centre user can view the Dashboard without selecting a customer and can view market watch and other functions such as In-job activities and News.

title: Customer authentication required for customer-specific activities like order placement and viewing order book/trade book
description: Verifies the rule that customer authentication is required before performing customer-specific activities (order placement, viewing order book or trade book). This reduces risk of unauthorized actions in a high-risk trading environment. Automation: MEDIUM (UI gating behavior).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, I attempt customer-specific activities without customer authentication and confirm the system requires customer authentication before those activities can be performed.
prerequisites: 1) Call Centre user account is active and can log in. 2) Orders, Order Book, and Trade Book functions are available in the environment. 3) At least one valid customer exists to authenticate for the positive continuation portion of the test.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open the application URL; verify the logon screen appears.
2. Log in with valid credentials and select a language; verify the Customer Authentication screen appears.
3. Do not authenticate a customer; verify no portfolio is selected.
4. Attempt to start order placement (open Orders menu and attempt to reach order entry); observe that customer authentication is required before proceeding with order placement.
5. Attempt to open Order Book (Orders/Order Book); observe that customer authentication is required before viewing the order book.
6. Attempt to open Trade Book; observe that customer authentication is required before viewing the trade book.
7. Now authenticate a customer (Service Mode + Identification Type/Number) and click Authenticate; verify the Portfolio List appears.
8. Select a portfolio and submit, then proceed into Trading; verify the user is now in authenticated customer context and can access customer-specific activities.
expectedResult:
1) Without customer authentication, customer-specific activities (order placement, viewing order book or trade book) require customer authentication.
2) After customer authentication and portfolio selection, the user can proceed into the authenticated customer context for those activities.
3) Abuse path ruled out: attempting customer-specific actions without authenticating a customer does not allow completing those actions.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Customer authentication is required to perform customer specific activities such as order placement, viewing order book or trade book

title: Open Dashboard from Trading screen after completing Logging on steps
description: Verifies the end-to-end navigation to open Dashboard from the Trading screen after completing the Logging on steps. This confirms the primary entry flow for dashboard viewing. Automation: HIGH (deterministic UI navigation).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, I complete the logging on steps, reach the Trading screen, and open the Dashboard by clicking Dashboard.

testDescription: As a Call Centre Operator placing a disclosed buy order, I need initial disclosed quantity and additional disclosed quantity fields to become enabled and require entry so the order can be prepared correctly.
prerequisites: 1) Call Centre user credentials exist (cc_user_01). 2) A test customer portfolio exists and is authenticated (PF-TEST-0001). 3) Buy Order Entry is accessible and supports Quantity Type selection (Regular/Disclosed).
stepsToPerform:
1. Open the application URL and verify the logon screen is displayed.
2. Login with 'cc_user_01' (masked password), language 'English'; verify Customer Authentication screen appears.
3. Authenticate customer using Portfolio Reference Number 'PF-TEST-0001', select a portfolio, and select Trading; verify Trading screen is displayed.
4. Open Buy Order Entry; verify Order Entry create screen is displayed.
5. Select a security (Symbol + Exchange) so order entry fields are active; verify Quantity Type control is visible.
6. Set Quantity Type to 'Disclosed' (Disclosed Order); verify 'initial disclosed quantity' and 'additional disclosed quantity' fields become enabled.
7. Enter initial disclosed quantity '100' and additional disclosed quantity '50'; verify both fields accept the input.
8. Switch Quantity Type back to 'Regular' and then again to 'Disclosed'; verify the disclosed quantity fields re-enable when Disclosed is selected.
9. Close Order Entry without placing an order; verify return to Trading screen.
expectedResult:
1) Selecting 'Disclosed Order' enables both 'initial disclosed quantity' and 'additional disclosed quantity' fields.
2) User can enter values into both enabled disclosed quantity fields.
3) Toggling Quantity Type away from and back to Disclosed results in fields being enabled again when Disclosed is selected.

sourceCitation.excerpt: if the user selects Disclosed Order, then  initial disclosed quantity and additional disclosed quantity field are enabled and user needs to fill it up.

title: Quantity Type Regular disables conditional qty1 and conditional qty2 input fields
description: Verifies that selecting Regular order disables Conditional qty1 and conditional qty2 fields, preventing unintended entry of conditional quantities for regular orders. Automation: MEDIUM (UI enable/disable assertions).
testDescription: As a Call Centre Operator placing a regular buy order, I need Conditional qty1 and conditional qty2 input fields to be disabled to match the regular order behavior.
prerequisites: 1) Call Centre user credentials exist (cc_user_01). 2) A test customer portfolio exists and is authenticated (PF-TEST-0001). 3) Buy Order Entry supports Quantity Type selection and shows Conditional qty1 and conditional qty2 input fields.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open the application URL and verify the logon screen is displayed.
2. Login with 'cc_user_01' (masked password), language 'English'; verify Customer Authentication screen appears.
3. Authenticate customer using Portfolio Reference Number 'PF-TEST-0001', select a portfolio, and select Trading; verify Trading screen is displayed.
4. Open Buy Order Entry; verify Order Entry create screen is displayed.
5. Select a security (Symbol + Exchange); verify Quantity Type control and fields 'Conditional qty1' and 'conditional qty2' are visible on the form.
6. Set Quantity Type to 'Regular'; verify 'Conditional qty1' and 'conditional qty2' input fields are disabled (non-editable).

title: Stop Loss order requires Trigger Price and Limit Price
description: Verifies that when placing a Buy order with Bid price Type set to Stop Loss Order, the user must provide both Trigger Price and Limit Price before proceeding. This protects correctness of stop-loss execution conditions. Automation: MEDIUM (UI validation dependent).
testDescription: As a Call Centre Operator, while creating an Equity Buy order, selecting Stop Loss Order as the bid price type must require both Trigger Price and Limit Price to be provided to proceed with order placement.
prerequisites: 1) Call Centre operator user is active and can log in via SSO. 2) A customer exists with at least one portfolio and is eligible for equity order placement. 3) At least one tradable equity security symbol exists for the selected exchange to reach order entry create screen. 4) Trading application is available and reachable in test environment.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open the application URL in a browser; verify the login screen is displayed.
2. Enter a valid test Login ID and Password and select language 'English'; click Login; verify the Customer Authentication screen appears.
3. Select Service Mode 'Phone', select Identification Type 'National Id', enter a synthetic Identification Number '999999999'; click Authenticate; verify a Portfolio List is displayed.
4. Select one portfolio row and click Submit; verify the integrated login options appear and select 'Trading'; verify the Trading screen (tiles) is displayed.
5. Navigate to Orders menu and open Order Entry; verify the Buy order entry Create phase screen is displayed.
6. Provide a Symbol (enter first three characters, then select from dropdown) and select an Exchange; verify the order entry create fields are available for input.
7. Set Bid price Type to 'Stop Loss Order'; verify Trigger Price and Limit Price fields are present for entry.
8. Enter Quantity '10' and leave Trigger Price blank; enter Limit Price '100.00'; click Place Order; verify the user cannot proceed (order does not move to Preview).
9. Enter Trigger Price '101.00' and clear Limit Price; click Place Order; verify the user cannot proceed (order does not move to Preview).
10. Enter both Trigger Price '101.00' and Limit Price '100.00'; click Place Order; verify the Preview screen appears (Create → Preview transition).
expectedResult:
1) With Bid price Type set to Stop Loss Order, clicking Place Order without Trigger Price does not move to Preview (Create remains active).
2) With Bid price Type set to Stop Loss Order, clicking Place Order without Limit Price does not move to Preview (Create remains active).
3) When both Trigger Price and Limit Price are provided, Place Order moves the flow to Preview screen showing order details.

sourceCitation.location: Placing a Buy Order Entry > Bid price Type (Lines L781-L785)
sourceCitation.excerpt: The Bid price Type is Stop Loss Order, user needs provide the Trigger Price and Limit Price.

testDataRequirements: Seed 3 test accounts with known balances in ILS: (A) Net=1000, Block=200, OD=400; (B) Net=1000, Block=1000, OD=400; (C) Net=1000, Block=1001, OD=400. Fund Balance UI must display Net Balance, Block Balance, OD Limit, and Available funds/Available Balance for these accounts.
prerequisites:
1) Test environment has a valid Call Centre user account with access to Trading module.
2) Three test customer portfolios exist and are selectable from Portfolio List after authentication.
3) Fund Balance data for the selected account is pre-seeded as: Account A Net Balance=1000 ILS, Block Balance=200 ILS, Overdraft Limit=400 ILS; Account B Net Balance=1000 ILS, Block Balance=1000 ILS, Overdraft Limit=400 ILS; Account C Net Balance=1000 ILS, Block Balance=1001 ILS, Overdraft Limit=400 ILS.
4) Application is reachable via browser URL and login is through SSO.
stepsToPerform:
1. Launch the application URL in a browser and verify the logon screen is displayed.
2. Enter valid Call Centre login ID/password, select language, click Login, and verify the Customer Authentication screen appears.
3. Select Service Mode and enter a synthetic Identification Type/Identification Number, click Authenticate, and verify a Portfolio List is displayed.
4. Select the portfolio for Account A (ACC-TEST-001) and click Submit; in integrated login options select Trading and verify the Trading screen tiles display.
5. Navigate to Account & Portfolio > Funds Balance, select Account A from the account dropdown and Currency=ILS, click Go, and verify the Fund Balance row shows Net Balance=1000 ILS, Block Balance=200 ILS, OD Limit=400 ILS.
6. Compute expected Available Balance = 1000 - 200 + 400 = 1200 ILS and verify the displayed Available Balance/Available funds equals 1200 ILS.
7. Repeat step 5 for Account B (ACC-TEST-002) with Net=1000, Block=1000, OD=400; compute expected Available Balance = 1000 - 1000 + 400 = 400 ILS and verify the displayed Available Balance/Available funds equals 400 ILS (boundary at Block=Net).
8. Repeat step 5 for Account C (ACC-TEST-003) with Net=1000, Block=1001, OD=400; compute expected Available Balance = 1000 - 1001 + 400 = 399 ILS and verify the displayed Available Balance/Available funds equals 399 ILS (just past boundary: Block>Net).
9. Close the Fund Balance window and verify no changes were made to the seeded balances (view again for one account to confirm same values).
expectedResult:
1) For Account A, Available Balance displayed equals 1200 ILS, matching 1000-200+400.
2) For boundary Account B (Block=Net), Available Balance displayed equals 400 ILS.
3) For just-past boundary Account C (Block>Net by 1), Available Balance displayed equals 399 ILS.

title: Verify DailyStockGL formula for Bond Class price calculation in Units
description: Verifies DailyStockGL calculation for Bond Class when price calculation is in Units using the documented formula, including boundary at Latest Net Price Change = 0 and just past it. testDescription: As a Call Centre user viewing portfolio valuation calculations for a bond class priced in Units, DailyStockGL must equal (Latest Net Price Change * Quantity * (PoolFactor/100)) / MajorMinFactor. Validate using concrete values at boundary and just past boundary.
dataMaskingNotes: Use synthetic security identifiers and portfolio reference; no real ISINs required.
testDataRequirements: Seed 2 valuation snapshots for a bond-class security in Unit mode with known components and expected DailyStockGL: Case A Latest Net Price Change=0.00, Quantity=100, PoolFactor=80, MajorMinFactor=10; Case B Latest Net Price Change=0.01, Quantity=100, PoolFactor=80, MajorMinFactor=10. Expected: A=0; B=(0.01*100*0.8)/10=0.08.
prerequisites:
1) Call Centre user can log in and access Portfolio Valuation.
2) Test customer portfolio includes a Bond Class security with "Price Calculation in Units" and exposes DailyStockGL and the required components (or provides them via a view used for calculations).
3) Valuation data for the bond security is seeded with: Quantity=100, PoolFactor=80, MajorMinFactor=10 and two Latest Net Price Change values (0.00 and 0.01) on selectable dates.
4) Portfolio Valuation screen shows Daily Gain/Loss output consistent with DailyStockGL for that bond class/security.
stepsToPerform:
1. Launch the application URL and verify login screen appears.
2. Log in with Call Centre credentials and verify Customer Authentication screen appears.
3. Authenticate the test customer and select the portfolio that contains the seeded bond security; choose Trading and verify Trading screen opens.
4. Navigate to Account & Portfolio > Portfolio Valuation and locate the seeded bond class security row.
5. Set valuation date to the snapshot where Latest Net Price Change=0.00 and refresh the list; verify the bond security row is present.
6. Compute expected DailyStockGL = (0.00 * 100 * (80/100)) / 10 = 0.00 and verify the displayed daily gain/loss value corresponding to DailyStockGL for that row equals 0.00.
7. Change valuation date to the snapshot where Latest Net Price Change=0.01 and refresh; verify the bond security row is present.
8. Compute expected DailyStockGL = (0.01 * 100 * 0.8) / 10 = 0.08 and verify the displayed daily gain/loss value corresponding to DailyStockGL for that row equals 0.08.
9. Re-select the first snapshot date again and verify the value returns to 0.00 (repeatability).
10. Close Portfolio Valuation screen.
expectedResult:
1) At boundary Latest Net Price Change=0.00, DailyStockGL displayed equals 0.00.
2) Just past boundary Latest Net Price Change=0.01, DailyStockGL displayed equals 0.08 for Quantity=100, PoolFactor=80, MajorMinFactor=10.
3) Switching dates changes the displayed DailyStockGL consistently with seeded inputs.
4) No portfolio state is modified; calculations are read-only display results.

title: Portfolio networth calculation statements displayed per spec (today vs yesterday)
description: Validates the Portfolio Net worth calculation statements and computes expected numeric results from concrete inputs to ensure displayed net worth aligns with the documented formulas. Automation: MEDIUM — requires controlled test data and UI value capture.
testDescription: As a QA/auditor, I want to verify the Portfolio Summary net worth values match the specified formulas for NetWorth today, NetWorth yesterday, and Portfolio Net worth difference.
prerequisites: 1) Ability to provision a test customer/portfolio with known values for Total Fund Balance, Block, Pending Block Amount, and Total Market Value Acc Curr for both today and yesterday (seeded in test environment). 2) Call-centre user can authenticate that customer and open Portfolio Summary. 3) The UI displays the components or the resulting net worth values needed for verification (ASSUMPTION: Portfolio Summary shows net-worth and change).
stepsToPerform:
1. Seed (or confirm seeded) portfolio values for TODAY: Total Fund Balance=10,000.00 ILS; Block=1,200.00 ILS; Pending Block Amount=300.00 ILS; Total Market Value Acc Curr=5,500.00 ILS.
2. Seed (or confirm seeded) portfolio values for YESTERDAY: Total Fund Balance=9,800.00 ILS; Block=1,000.00 ILS; Pending Block Amount=250.00 ILS; Total Market Value Acc Curr=5,200.00 ILS.
3. Compute expected NetWorth today using the documented formula: 10,000.00 - 1,200.00 + 300.00 + 5,500.00 = 14,600.00 ILS.
4. Compute expected NetWorth yesterday: 9,800.00 - 1,000.00 + 250.00 + 5,200.00 = 14,250.00 ILS.
5. Compute expected Portfolio Net worth (difference): 14,600.00 - 14,250.00 = 350.00 ILS.
6. Open the application URL and log in with valid call-centre credentials; verify Customer Authentication screen appears.
7. Authenticate the seeded customer (using synthetic Portfolio Reference Number 'PRN-TEST-NW-01'); select the portfolio and enter 'Trading'.
8. Navigate to Account & Portfolio and open 'Portfolio Summary'; capture the displayed net-worth today value.
9. Capture the displayed change in net-worth compared to a day before.
10. Compare captured UI values to expected calculations and record evidence (screenshots/export if available); then close the Portfolio Summary screen.
expectedResult:
1) Displayed net-worth today equals 14,600.00 ILS for the seeded dataset.
2) Displayed change in net-worth compared to a day before equals 350.00 ILS (Networth today – Networth yesterday).
3) The calculation basis matches the documented expressions for NetWorth today and NetWorth Yesterday (components align to Total Fund Balance – Block + Pending Block Amount + Total Market Value Acc Curr).

sourceCitation.excerpt: Portfolio Net worth = Networth today – Networth yesterday

title: Market Watch dynamically updates via broadcast feed and shows delay message at bottom when delayed
description: Verifies market watch resilience to delayed market data by checking that dynamic broadcast feed updates are reflected and that a delay message is displayed at the bottom of the screen when the feed is delayed. Automation: LOW-MEDIUM — requires controllable market data feed delay injection or test environment toggle.
testDescription: As a call-centre user, I want Market Watch to update dynamically with broadcast feed changes and clearly indicate when data is delayed so I can interpret prices correctly.
prerequisites: 1) Call-centre user can access Market Watch. 2) Test environment supports simulating broadcast feed delay (e.g., toggling delay on market data adapter) without impacting unrelated services. 3) Market Watch contains at least one actively updating security (synthetic 'SEC_LIVE').
stepsToPerform:
1. Open the application URL and log in with valid call-centre credentials.

3. Observe at least one market field on 'SEC_LIVE' (e.g., LTP or Bid/Offer) for 30 seconds; verify at least one value or color change occurs indicating dynamic update.
4. Record the observed value/time for evidence.
5. Inject a broadcast feed delay in the test environment for the exchange feed (failure mode: delayed feed) while keeping the application session active.
6. Return focus to the Market Watch screen and wait up to 60 seconds.
7. Verify a delay message is displayed at the bottom of the market watch screen.
8. Remove/disable the injected delay to restore normal feed.
9. Verify the delay message disappears (or is no longer shown) and market watch resumes dynamic updates.
10. Close the Market Watch screen.
expectedResult:

2) When feed is delayed, a delay message is displayed on the bottom of the Market Watch screen.

title: Top Gainers/Losers supports criteria selection and cutoff upper limit (exclude above cutoff)
description: Validates that Top Gainers/Losers supports selecting a criteria and that the cutoff acts as an upper limit so values above cutoff are not displayed. This protects correctness of market ranking screens where users rely on filtered movers lists. Automation: MEDIUM (UI grid assertions).
testDescription: As a Call Centre user, I want to select a criteria for Top Gainers/Losers and apply a cutoff value so that results above the cutoff are excluded from the displayed spreadsheet.
prerequisites: 1) Call Centre application URL is reachable and user has a valid SSO login. 2) Market data feed is available for at least one Exchange (e.g., TASE) with enough securities to show a list in Top Gainers/Losers. 3) Tester knows a concrete cutoff value X and can visually identify at least one displayed row value <= X and at least one candidate row value that would be > X if not filtered (use same column as chosen criteria).
stepsToPerform:
1. Open the Call Centre application URL in a supported browser and confirm the login screen is displayed.
2. Enter a valid login ID and password, select language (English), click Login, and confirm the Customer Authentication screen appears.
3. From the integrated login options, select Trading and confirm the Trading screen (tiles) is displayed.
4. Navigate to Market View → Top Gainers/Losers and confirm the Top Gainers & Losers window opens.
5. Select an Exchange from the drop down (e.g., TASE) and confirm the exchange selection is reflected on the screen.
6. Select a Criteria for displaying the data (e.g., "LTP % change") and confirm the selected criteria is shown in the criteria control.
7. In the cutoff input, enter a numeric cutoff value X (boundary test): set X to a value that will include some rows (e.g., X=1.50) and confirm the cutoff field shows X.
8. Click Go and confirm the data is displayed in the available spread sheet.
9. Verify in the resulting spreadsheet that every displayed row's value in the selected criteria column is <= X (e.g., no row shows LTP % change > 1.50).
10. Boundary just past the limit: change the cutoff to X-0.01 (e.g., 1.49), click Go, and confirm any rows with value equal to the previous boundary (e.g., 1.50) are no longer displayed while rows <= 1.49 remain.
11. Click Close and confirm the Top Gainers/Losers window closes.
expectedResult:
1) After clicking Go, data is displayed in the spreadsheet for the selected Exchange and Criteria.
2) The cutoff value acts as an upper limit: rows with criteria value above the cutoff are not displayed.
3) Boundary behavior is respected: at cutoff X rows with value <= X can appear, and when reduced just past the boundary (X-0.01) rows above the new cutoff are excluded.
4) Window closes on Close action.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Enter the cutoff value, which marks the upper limit of the results i.e. data above this cutoff value is not displayed.

testDescription: As a user initiating Security Transfer with multiple positions in different instrument currencies, the system should convert each record's value to portfolio currency and show a consolidated transfer value equal to the sum of converted individual values.
prerequisites: 1) Customer portfolio currency is ILS. 2) Portfolio has at least two settled positions visible in Add Security: Security A in ILX with Previous closing Price=100.00 and Available Quantity=10; Security B in USD with Previous closing Price=20.00 and Available Quantity=5. 3) Exchange rate available for Security B conversion is 1 USD = 3.50 ILS (configured/available for the test Business Date). 4) Security Transfer screen shows Total Transfer Value/Transfer Value in account/portfolio currency as per product behavior.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open the application URL, log in with valid credentials, and verify Customer Authentication screen appears.
2. Authenticate the customer and select the correct portfolio; choose Trading and verify Trading tiles screen is displayed.
3. Navigate to Transfers and open Security Transfer; verify Add Security/Select Security screen appears with positions list.
4. Select Security A row and verify Transfer Quantity defaults to Available Quantity (10) and Value is shown for the row.
5. Select Security B row and verify Transfer Quantity defaults to Available Quantity (5) and Value is shown for the row.
6. Set/confirm Transfer Quantity for Security A = 10 and for Security B = 5 (leave defaults) and observe the displayed per-row Value values.
7. Compute expected values: Security A value in instrument currency = 10 * 100.00 = 1000.00 ILX; Security B value in instrument currency = 5 * 20.00 = 100.00 USD; converted Security B value in portfolio currency = 100.00 * 3.50 = 350.00 ILS; consolidated expected = 1000.00 + 350.00 = 1350.00 ILS.
8. Verify the UI displays a consolidated/total transfer value in portfolio currency equal to 1350.00 ILS for the selected records.
9. Proceed to the next step (Add Beneficiary) and return/back to Add Security if needed; verify the consolidated transfer value remains consistent with selected records.
10. Cancel the transfer flow to avoid creating a transfer request (cleanup).
expectedResult:
1) Selected positions are available in Add Security (implying positions were fetched) and per-row Value is displayed.
2) The consolidated transfer value displayed in portfolio currency equals the sum of individual record values converted to portfolio currency (for the provided test data: 1350.00 ILS).
3) Values are shown in portfolio currency at consolidated level as described and remain consistent while records remain selected.

title: TASE Self-Transaction blocking applies at Continuous phase for TASE securities
description: Verifies that the system blocks self-transactions specifically at the Continuous phase for securities traded in TASE, preventing prohibited matching against the customer's own open order. Automation: MEDIUM — UI order placement with deterministic data setup.
testDescription: As a customer (via Call Centre order entry), when an opposite order would create a self-transaction during the Continuous phase on TASE, the system blocks the order and does not allow placement.
prerequisites: 1) Test environment configured with a TASE equity/security where 'Phase' can be observed as 'Continuous' in Order Entry UI. 2) A BP/customer exists with an account/portfolio eligible to trade the selected TASE security. 3) There is an existing open order for the BP in the same security on the same day that is not fully executed yet (e.g., open Sell order with remaining quantity).
stepsToPerform:
1. Launch the Call Centre application in a browser; verify the logon screen appears.
2. Log in with a valid Call Centre user (e.g., cc_trader_01) and select English; verify access to Trading screen.
3. Authenticate/select the target customer context if required (Customer Authentication → select portfolio → Submit → choose Trading); verify Trading tiles are shown.
4. Navigate to Orders → Order Entry; verify the equity order entry Create phase is displayed.
5. Select the TASE exchange and the target TASE security symbol; verify the order entry shows the security details including the displayed 'Phase' field.
6. Verify the displayed phase for the selected TASE security is 'Continuous' (as precondition for this test).
7. Attempt to place an opposite order that would self-transaction against the existing open order (e.g., if existing order is Sell, attempt a Buy that meets the self-transaction criteria); click Place Order.
8. Observe the system response; verify the order is blocked (no transition to Preview/Confirmation for a placed order).
9. Capture the error presented to the user and verify it indicates self-transactions are not allowed for TASE.
10. Close the order entry or reset the form; verify no new opposite order was created for this BP/security for today (e.g., check Order Book does not show a new order in Pending/Transit).
expectedResult:
1) When phase is Continuous and the attempted order qualifies as a self-transaction, the system blocks the order and does not allow placement.
2) User is shown the specified self-transaction error message (validated in detail in TC-TASE-ST-05).
3) No new opposite order record is created/visible for the attempted blocked submission (e.g., absent from Order Book for that BP/security/day).

title: Block opposite Buy against open Sell when new Buy is MKT or limit price >= open Sell price; show error message
description: Verifies the specific self-transaction blocking branch when an open Sell exists and the user attempts a Buy that would cross (MKT or limit >= open sell price). Includes boundary at limit price equal to open sell price and just below it. Automation: MEDIUM — requires known open sell price and open order state.
testDescription: With an existing open Sell order (not fully executed) for a TASE security, attempt to place a new Buy order as MKT and as Limit at/around the open Sell price and verify the system blocks per rule.
prerequisites: 1) For BP_TEST_02, there is an existing open Sell order in TASE for Symbol=TASE_EQ_XYZ, dated today, not fully executed, with open Sell price = 100.00 (ILS) and remaining quantity > 0. 2) The security is in Continuous phase at time of test. 3) Call Centre user has permission to place equity orders for BP_TEST_02.
stepsToPerform:
1. Launch the Call Centre application; verify the logon screen appears.
2. Log in as Call Centre user (e.g., cc_trader_03) with English language.
3. Authenticate/select BP_TEST_02 portfolio and enter Trading context.
4. Open Equity Order Book; filter Exchange=TASE, Instrument=Equity, Symbol=TASE_EQ_XYZ; click Go; verify the open Sell order exists and note open Sell price = 100.00.
5. Navigate to Orders → Order Entry; select Exchange=TASE and Symbol=TASE_EQ_XYZ; verify the order entry Create screen shows Phase as Continuous.
6. Attempt #1 (MKT): set side=Buy and choose Market (MKT) as order type/price type as applicable; enter Quantity=10; click Place Order; verify the system blocks the order.
7. Clear/reset the form; verify you can start a new order entry for the same symbol.
8. Attempt #2 (Boundary equal): set side=Buy, set order type=Limit, set Price=100.00 (equal to open Sell price), Quantity=10; click Place Order; verify the system blocks the order.
9. Attempt #3 (Just below boundary): set side=Buy, set order type=Limit, set Price=99.99 (just below open Sell price), Quantity=10; click Place Order; verify the system does not block due to this specific condition and allows progress to the next phase (Preview) or proceeds per normal flow.
10. Cleanup: If Attempt #3 progressed to Preview, click Back/Cancel to avoid creating a real order; verify no new Buy order was confirmed/created from Attempt #3 in Order Book.
expectedResult:
1) Buy MKT attempt is blocked when an existing open Sell is present; user receives the specified self-transaction error message.
2) Buy Limit attempt with limit price equal to the open Sell price (100.00) is blocked; user receives the specified self-transaction error message.
3) Buy Limit attempt with limit price just below the open Sell price (99.99) is not blocked by this specific condition and can proceed (then tester cancels to avoid state creation).

title: Delayed Data configured as 15 mins for foreign and local securities data per subscription
description: Verifies the system enforces a configured 15-minute delay for market data for both foreign and local securities as per user subscription, by comparing displayed timestamps/values against a reference live feed. testDescription: As a subscribed user, when viewing securities data for both local and foreign securities, the displayed data reflects a 15-minute delay configuration.
prerequisites: 1) Environment has delayed market data feature enabled with configured delay = 15 minutes for both foreign and local securities data. 2) A test user subscription is set such that delayed data applies. 3) A trusted reference 'live' market data source/feed is available to testers for the same symbols (for comparison). 4) Two test symbols exist: one local (TASE) and one foreign (Orbis/foreign exchange).

5. From the reference live feed, record the live timestamp and the value that corresponds to exactly 15 minutes before 'now' (T_live_minus_15) for the same symbol; capture the live value at T_live_minus_15 (LTP_live_minus_15_local).
6. Verify T_app_local aligns to approximately 15 minutes behind current live time (difference = 15 minutes ± 60 seconds) and LTP_app_local matches (or is consistent with) LTP_live_minus_15_local.

title: Delayed Data delay time is configurable in BαNCS ORS system and can be updated on request
description: Verifies operational resilience of delayed-data configuration change: after updating the delay in BαNCS ORS system (on request), the application reflects the new delay for both foreign and local data. Automation: LOW — requires configuration change coordination and time-based verification.
testDescription: As an operator/tester, when the delay time is updated in BαNCS ORS system, the market data delay observed in the application changes accordingly without requiring code changes.
prerequisites: 1) Access/coordination is available to update delayed-data configuration in BαNCS ORS system. 2) A test user subscription exists where delayed data applies. 3) Reference live market data source is available for comparison. 4) Two symbols exist: one local (TASE) and one foreign.
stepsToPerform:
1. Launch the Call Centre application; verify logon screen appears.
2. Log in as delayed-data subscribed user (e.g., cc_md_delay_02) using English.
3. Baseline check: open market data for a local symbol and record observed application timestamp/value; verify it is delayed by 15 minutes (per current configuration).
4. Baseline check: open market data for a foreign symbol and record observed application timestamp/value; verify it is delayed by 15 minutes.
5. Coordinate/configure change in BαNCS ORS system to update delay time from 15 minutes to 10 minutes (requested update); record the exact change time (T_change).
6. After configuration is applied (and after allowing for propagation if needed), refresh/reopen the same local symbol market data screen; record new observed application timestamp (T_app_local_new).
7. Validate the new delay for local symbol is 10 minutes ± 60 seconds relative to live/reference time.
8. Refresh/reopen the foreign symbol market data screen; record new observed application timestamp (T_app_foreign_new).

10. Restore configuration back to 15 minutes in BαNCS ORS system as cleanup; refresh once more to confirm delay returns to 15 minutes ± 60 seconds.
expectedResult:
1) After updating the delay time in BαNCS ORS system, the application reflects the new delay for local securities data.
2) After updating the delay time in BαNCS ORS system, the application reflects the new delay for foreign securities data.
